introduction_markdown: Multiple choice paper (June 2023, Ordinary Level, 0570 Mathematics 1, one and a half hours). Answer ALL 50 questions; all questions carry equal marks. Each question has four suggested answers A, B, C and D; mark only one answer for each question. Non-programmable calculators are allowed.
enonce_intro_markdown: **Multiple choice questions** - choose the one correct answer, A, B, C or D.

questions.enonce_markdown: The value of the digit 7 in $64.176$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: After the decimal point the places are tenths, hundredths, thousandths. In $64.176$ the digit 1 is in the tenths place, 7 is in the hundredths place and 6 in the thousandths place. So the digit 7 stands for $\frac{7}{100}$. The trap is to pick $\frac{7}{10}$ by taking 7 as the first decimal digit. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The H.C.F of $2^3\times 3$ and $2\times 3^2\times 5$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The H.C.F is the product of the prime factors common to both numbers, each taken with the smaller power. For 2: the powers are $2^3$ and $2^1$, so take $2^1$. For 3: the powers are $3^1$ and $3^2$, so take $3^1$. The factor 5 appears only in the second number, so it is left out. H.C.F $=2\times 3$ ($=6$). Option B is the L.C.M without the factor 5, and D is not even a divisor of the first number. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The numbers $0.5,\ 0.4,\ 0,\ 0.25$ arranged in ascending order gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Ascending means from the smallest to the largest. Write all numbers with two decimal places: $0.50,\ 0.40,\ 0.00,\ 0.25$. The order is $0.00<0.25<0.40<0.50$, that is $0,\ 0.25,\ 0.4,\ 0.5$. Option C is the descending order. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The number line that represents the set $Q=\{-1<x\leq 3\}$ is

![fig-1](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_1.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: In $-1<x\leq 3$ the end $-1$ is not included (strict sign $<$), so it is drawn with an open circle. The end $3$ is included (sign $\leq$), so it is drawn with a filled circle. Only line D has an open circle on the left end and a filled circle on the right end. Line A has two open circles, line B two filled circles, and line C has the two types the wrong way round. (The right-hand label of each line is printed as $-3$ in the paper; it is clearly meant to be $3$.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number, $\sqrt{7}$, belongs to the set of
questions.corrige_markdown: $7$ is not a perfect square ($2^2=4$ and $3^2=9$), so $\sqrt{7}=2.6457\ldots$ is a non-terminating, non-recurring decimal. It cannot be written as a fraction of two integers, so it is an irrational number. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The fraction "four-thirds" in figures is
questions.corrige_markdown: "Four-thirds" means 4 parts, each a third of a whole: $\frac{4}{3}$. Option B is four and one third, option C is 4 cubed ($64$) and option D equals $4\div\frac{1}{3}=12$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $0.00078$ can be written as $a\times 10^n$, where $1<a<10$, then the value of $n$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Move the decimal point to just after the first non-zero digit: $0.00078=7.8\times 10^{-4}$, because the point moves 4 places to the right (a number smaller than 1 gives a negative power). So $a=7.8$ and $n=-4$. The trap is to count only 3 zeros and answer $-3$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number, $1949.46$ to the nearest whole number is
questions.corrige_markdown: Look at the first decimal digit: it is 4, which is less than 5, so we round down and keep $1949$. Options C and D round to the nearest ten and the nearest hundred, which is not what is asked. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: In a class of $90$ students, $25$ are boys. The ratio of girls to boys is
questions.corrige_markdown: Number of girls $=90-25=65$. Ratio girls : boys $=65:25$. Divide both terms by 5: $13:5$. Take care with the order: girls come first, so $5:13$ (boys : girls) is wrong. Option A, $5:18$, is the ratio of boys to the whole class ($25:90$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The simple interest on $200{,}000$ FCFA at a rate of $3\%$ after 5 years is
questions.corrige_markdown: Use $I=\frac{P\times R\times T}{100}$ with the rate taken per year: $I=\frac{200000\times 3\times 5}{100}=30000$ FCFA. (The interest of one year alone would be $6{,}000$ FCFA; the interest of 5 years is five times that.) **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the sets $P=\{1,3,5,6\}$ and $Q=\{2,4,7,8\}$, then $n(P\cap Q)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $P$ and $Q$ have no element in common, so $P\cap Q=\varnothing$, the empty set. $n(P\cap Q)$ is the NUMBER of elements of $P\cap Q$, which is $0$. Options A and D are sets with one element, and C is a set, not a number. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the sets $F=\{\text{football players}\}$ and $G=\{\text{girls}\}$, the set notation for the statement "All girls play football" is
questions.corrige_markdown: If every girl is a football player, then every element of $G$ is also an element of $F$: $G$ is a subset of $F$, written $G\subset F$. Option D reverses this and would mean that all football players are girls. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In set notation, the shaded region in figure 1 is

![fig-2](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_2.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The shaded part lies inside $P$ but outside $Q$ (the overlap of the two circles is not shaded). "Inside $P$ and not in $Q$" is $P\cap Q'$. $P'\cap Q$ would be the part of $Q$ outside $P$, $P\cap Q$ is the overlap, and $Q'\cup P$ would include everything outside $Q$ as well as all of $P$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that p: Adamu is hard working, q: Adamu is brilliant. The compound statement "Adamu is hard working and brilliant" is
questions.corrige_markdown: Two statements joined by "and" form a conjunction, written $p\wedge q$. A disjunction uses "or" ($p\vee q$) and an implication uses "if ... then" ($p\Rightarrow q$). "Proposition" only means any single statement that is true or false, so it does not name the way the two are joined. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: For any function $f$, $f^{-1}$ always maps its
questions.corrige_markdown: $f$ takes an element of its domain to an element of its range. The inverse function undoes this, so $f^{-1}$ takes an element of the range of $f$ back to the domain of $f$. In short, $f^{-1}$ maps the range of $f$ to the domain of $f$. Option C describes $f$ itself. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f:x\mapsto 2x+5$, then $f(-3)$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Replace $x$ by $-3$: $f(-3)=2(-3)+5=-6+5=-1$. The trap is to lose the sign and compute $6+5$ or $-6-5$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $f(x)=x$ and $g(x)=3x-2$, then the composite function $gf(x)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: $gf(x)=g(f(x))$: first apply $f$, then $g$. Since $f(x)=x$, $gf(x)=g(x)=3x-2$. Option A is the product $f(x)\times g(x)$, not the composition. Options B and D look like inverse functions, not compositions. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The distance from the centre of a circle to any point on the circumference is called
questions.corrige_markdown: A segment joining the centre to a point of the circle is a radius. A chord joins two points of the circle, a diameter is a chord through the centre (twice the radius), and an arc is a part of the circumference. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the exterior angle of a regular polygon is $30^\circ$, then its interior angle is
questions.corrige_markdown: An interior angle and the exterior angle at the same vertex lie on a straight line, so they add up to $180^\circ$. Interior angle $=180^\circ-30^\circ=150^\circ$. (The polygon has $\frac{360}{30}=12$ sides, which is where the distractor 12 comes from.) **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The regular solid figure represented by the net in figure 2 is called

![fig-3](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_3.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The net is made of 6 identical squares: a row of four with one square above and one below. Folded, it forms a solid with 6 equal square faces, a cube. A cuboid has rectangular faces that are not all equal, a cylinder has circular faces, and a square is a plane shape, not a solid. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The constructions shown in figure 3 are such that $PQ$ is the perpendicular bisector of $RS$. The value of the angle $PTS$ is

![fig-4](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_4.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: A perpendicular bisector cuts the segment $RS$ at its midpoint $T$ and meets it at a right angle. So angle $PTS=90^\circ$. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
In figure 4, the value of angle $p$ is

![fig-5](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_5.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The two horizontal lines are parallel (see the arrows). At the top line, the slanted line makes an angle of $50^\circ$ with the right-hand direction of the line, measured below the line. At the lower line the corresponding angle (same position, below the line to the right of the slanted line) is also $50^\circ$. The angle $p$ is above the lower line, between its right-hand direction and the upward part of the slanted line, so it forms a straight-line pair with that $50^\circ$ angle: $p=180^\circ-50^\circ=130^\circ$. A common slip is to answer $50^\circ$ by treating $p$ as a corresponding angle of the marked angle. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The perimeter of a rectangle is $24$ cm. Given its width is $5$ cm, then its length is
questions.corrige_markdown: Perimeter $=2(\text{length}+\text{width})$, so $2(l+5)=24$, $l+5=12$ and $l=7$ cm. Check: $2(7+5)=24$. The trap is to forget that the perimeter contains two lengths and two widths, for example by subtracting only one width ($24-5=19$) or by forgetting to halve the perimeter first. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $\pi=\frac{22}{7}$ and the radius of a circle is $7$ cm, then the area of the circle is
questions.corrige_markdown: Area $=\pi r^2=\frac{22}{7}\times 7^2=\frac{22}{7}\times 49=22\times 7=154\ \text{cm}^2$. Option A is the circumference $2\pi r=44$ cm, and option C is twice the area ($2\pi r^2$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the volume of a cube is $64\ \text{cm}^3$, then each side has length
questions.corrige_markdown: Volume of a cube $=s^3$, so $s=\sqrt[3]{64}=4$ cm, because $4^3=64$. Option C comes from taking the square root ($\sqrt{64}=8$) instead of the cube root. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: On the Cartesian plane, the line $y=0$ is called the
questions.corrige_markdown: Every point of the horizontal axis has $y$-coordinate $0$, so the line $y=0$ is the $x$-axis. The $y$-axis is the line $x=0$. The origin is the single point $(0,0)$ and the ordinate is the $y$-coordinate of a point. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the lines $L_1: y=-3x+3$ and $L_2: y=mx-2$, such that $L_1$ is parallel to $L_2$, the value of $m$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Both lines are written as $y=mx+c$, so the coefficient of $x$ is the gradient. $L_1$ has gradient $-3$. Parallel lines have equal gradients, so $m=-3$. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The $x$-coordinate of the mid-point $M(x,y)$ of the points $P(0,3)$ and $Q(4,-3)$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The mid-point has coordinates $\left(\frac{x_1+x_2}{2},\frac{y_1+y_2}{2}\right)$. So $x=\frac{0+4}{2}=2$ (and $y=\frac{3+(-3)}{2}=0$, so $M=(2,0)$). **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The number of terms in the expression $2ax+3by-1$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Terms are separated by $+$ or $-$ signs: $2ax$, $3by$ and $-1$. There are 3 terms. The trap is to count letters or symbols. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Simplifying $2^5\times 2^{-3}$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: When multiplying powers of the same base, add the indices: $2^5\times 2^{-3}=2^{5+(-3)}=2^{2}$ ($=4$). Option A multiplies the indices ($5\times -3$), and option D subtracts them the wrong way ($-3-5$). **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Simplifying $3x-6y-2x$ gives
questions.corrige_markdown: Collect the like terms in $x$: $3x-2x=x$. The term $-6y$ is unchanged. The result is $x-6y$. Option C comes from adding $3x+2x$ instead of subtracting. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $P=\frac{E}{WL}$, an expression for $W$ in terms of $P$, $E$ and $L$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Multiply both sides by $WL$: $PWL=E$. Divide both sides by $PL$: $W=\frac{E}{PL}$. Check with numbers: $E=12$, $W=2$, $L=3$ give $P=\frac{12}{6}=2$, and $\frac{E}{PL}=\frac{12}{2\times 3}=2=W$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The next term in the sequence $3,\ 5,\ 8,\ 12,\ \ldots$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Look at the differences: $5-3=2$, $8-5=3$, $12-8=4$. The differences go up by 1 each time, so the next difference is 5 and the next term is $12+5=17$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The range of values of $x$ for which $7+2x<11$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Subtract 7 from both sides: $2x<4$. Divide by 2 (a positive number, so the sign is kept): $x<2$. The inequality is strict, so $2$ itself is not included (that rules out A). Check: $x=2$ gives $7+4=11$, which is not less than 11. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that the speed, $V$, of a car is inversely proportional to the time, $t$, then the equation relating $V$ to $t$, where $k$ is a constant is
questions.corrige_markdown: "$V$ is inversely proportional to $t$" means $V\propto\frac{1}{t}$, so $V=\frac{k}{t}$ for a constant $k$ (equivalently $Vt=k$). Option B is direct variation. Option D gives $V=\frac{1}{kt}$, which is not the standard form of inverse variation. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The number of regions in the network in figure 5 is

![fig-6](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_6.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The network has vertices $S,P,T,R,Q$ ($V=5$) and edges $SP$, $ST$, $TQ$, $PT$, $TR$, $RQ$ ($E=6$). The regions are the triangle $SPT$, the triangle $TRQ$ and the outside region (the region around the whole network counts as a region). Euler's formula $V-E+R=2$ gives $R=2-5+6=3$. The trap is to forget the outside region and answer 2. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The longest side in a right-angled triangle is
questions.corrige_markdown: The side facing the right angle is called the hypotenuse, and it is always the longest side (Pythagoras: $c^2=a^2+b^2$). Opposite and adjacent are names relative to a chosen angle, and acute describes an angle, not a side. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given that $\sin A=\frac{2}{3}$. The cosine of the angle complementary to angle $A$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: The complement of $A$ is $90^\circ-A$. For complementary angles $\cos(90^\circ-A)=\sin A$. So the required cosine is $\frac{2}{3}$. (In a right-angled triangle, the side opposite $A$ is the side adjacent to the other acute angle, so the two ratios are equal.) Option D is impossible, since a cosine never exceeds 1. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
The angle of elevation of $Q$ from $P$, in figure 6 is

![fig-7](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_7.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The angle of elevation of $Q$ from $P$ is the angle at $P$ between the horizontal line $PR$ and the line of sight $PQ$. In the figure this angle is marked $65^\circ$. The $35^\circ$ is the angle at $Q$, and the $90^\circ$ is the right angle at $R$. The trap is to choose the angle at $Q$. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the vectors $\mathbf{p}=\begin{pmatrix}2\\-1\end{pmatrix}$ and $\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}-2\\-3\end{pmatrix}$, then $\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{r}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Subtract component by component: $\mathbf{p}-\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}2-(-2)\\-1-(-3)\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}4\\2\end{pmatrix}$. Option A is the SUM $\mathbf{p}+\mathbf{r}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\-4\end{pmatrix}$, which is the usual trap when the minus sign is overlooked. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Given the vectors $\overrightarrow{PQ}$ and $\overrightarrow{QR}$ in figure 7, then $\overrightarrow{PR}$ is

![fig-8](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_8.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: By the triangle law, $\overrightarrow{PR}=\overrightarrow{PQ}+\overrightarrow{QR}$. In the figure the arrow on $a$ points from $P$ to $Q$, so $\overrightarrow{PQ}=a$. The arrow on $b$ points upwards, from $R$ to $Q$, so $b=\overrightarrow{RQ}$ and therefore $\overrightarrow{QR}=-b$. Hence $\overrightarrow{PR}=a+(-b)=a-b$. Reading the arrows carefully is the point of the question: if $b$ had been drawn from $Q$ to $R$, the answer would be $a+b$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: Given the vector $\overrightarrow{OM}=2\mathbf{i}+3\mathbf{j}$, the direction of this vector is
questions.corrige_markdown: The vector has horizontal component 2 and vertical component 3. The direction is the angle $\theta$ the vector makes with the positive $x$-axis: $\tan\theta=\frac{\text{vertical}}{\text{horizontal}}=\frac{3}{2}$, so $\theta=\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{3}{2}\right)\approx 56.3^\circ$. Option A inverts the ratio, and option C is a tangent value, not an angle. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The leading diagonal elements of the matrix $P$, where $P=\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\4&5\end{pmatrix}$ are
questions.corrige_markdown: The leading (main) diagonal runs from the top-left to the bottom-right corner: the elements are $2$ and $5$. The elements $3$ and $4$ lie on the other diagonal. **Answer: A.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The determinant of the matrix $\begin{pmatrix}4&5\\1&2\end{pmatrix}$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: For $\begin{pmatrix}a&b\\c&d\end{pmatrix}$ the determinant is $ad-bc$. Here $4\times 2-5\times 1=8-5=3$. Option A comes from subtracting in the wrong order ($bc-ad$). **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The translation $\begin{pmatrix}5\\-7\end{pmatrix}$ maps the $y$-coordinate of the point $(2,5)$ to
questions.corrige_markdown: A translation $\begin{pmatrix}a\\b\end{pmatrix}$ adds $a$ to the $x$-coordinate and $b$ to the $y$-coordinate. The image of $(2,5)$ is $(2+5,\ 5+(-7))=(7,-2)$. The new $y$-coordinate is $-2$. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown: $\begin{pmatrix}5\\7\end{pmatrix}-\begin{pmatrix}5\\-2\end{pmatrix}=$
questions.corrige_markdown: Subtract the components: top $5-5=0$, bottom $7-(-2)=7+2=9$. The result is $\begin{pmatrix}0\\9\end{pmatrix}$. Option C comes from writing $7-2$ and forgetting the double negative. **Answer: B.**

questions.enonce_markdown:
Figure 8 represents

![fig-9](gce-ol-maths-2023-p1-officiel-cameroun_exercice_1_fig_9.png)
questions.corrige_markdown: The figure shows rectangular bars on labelled categories $P,Q,R,S,T$ whose heights give the quantities: it is a bar chart. A pie chart uses sectors of a circle, a pictogram uses small pictures or symbols, and frequency is a quantity, not a type of diagram. **Answer: C.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The most popular mark scored in a test is called
questions.corrige_markdown: The most frequent value of a set of data (the one that occurs most often) is the mode. The median is the middle value, the mean is the average, and data is just the collection of marks. **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The median of the scores $3,\ 4,\ 1,\ 2,\ 2$ is
questions.corrige_markdown: Arrange the 5 scores in order: $1,\ 2,\ 2,\ 3,\ 4$. The median is the middle (3rd) value, which is $2$. The trap is to take the middle of the unordered list (the value 1) or to give the mean ($2.4$). **Answer: D.**

questions.enonce_markdown: The probability that Mary passes a test is $\frac{2}{3}$. The probability that she fails the test is
questions.corrige_markdown: Passing and failing are complementary events, so the probabilities add up to 1: $P(\text{fail})=1-\frac{2}{3}=\frac{1}{3}$. **Answer: A.**
